recognize_zh: 中央的嗜中性球有分葉核，胞質內散布多個金黃色、具折光性的短棒狀結晶；右下另一顆白血球核上也有少數金黃色結晶，背景紅血球多呈鋸齒狀，符合重度高膽紅素血症時白血球內的膽紅素結晶。
features: Neutrophil with lobulated nucleus containing multiple golden-yellow, refractile, short rod/needle-shaped cytoplasmic crystals
Crystals overlie both nucleus and cytoplasm and are not stained purple (intrinsic pigment color)
A second leukocyte (lower right) with dense nucleus shows a few similar yellow crystals
Background red cells are crenated (echinocytic) with small refractile artifacts; no other inclusions evident
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows crenated red cells and scattered leukocytes. A neutrophil in the center contains numerous golden-yellow, refractile, rod-shaped intracytoplasmic crystals that retain their natural color rather than taking up the stain; a second leukocyte shows a few similar crystals. Findings are consistent with intracellular bilirubin crystals, typically seen in smears from patients with marked hyperbilirubinemia, particularly neonates, and are thought to form in vitro after blood collection.

ddx.vs: Hemosiderin forms golden-brown to blue-black granular clumps that stain with Prussian blue, whereas bilirubin crystals are bright yellow needles/rods and iron-negative.
Hemozoin is brown-black and granular, and accompanies intraerythrocytic parasites, not bright yellow refractile rods.
Cryoglobulin deposits are pale blue-gray amorphous or crystalline material, whereas these crystals are distinctly golden-yellow and correlate with serum bilirubin.
Stain precipitate is purple-black, lies over cells and background alike, and is not confined to leukocyte cytoplasm.
